title: Anglo-Peabody mine tussle leaves Indonesian mining firm seeking new coal assets
body: PT Buma Internasional is still on the hunt for coal assets, as uncertainty lingers about its planned purchase of a stake in the Dawson project.

title: South32 sees limited risk of Indonesia replicating nickel success in alumina
body: South32 reported a 75% surge in full-year profit on Thursday, helped by strong performance at its alumina division and higher commodity prices.

title: Freeport Indonesia to wrap up Gresik plant repairs by early September
body: Freeport expects to complete early next month repair work at its JV smelter in East Java.

title: Indonesia scraps coal pricing rules after pushback from buyers
body: Miners will now be allowed to sell below government-set benchmarks.

title: Freeport Indonesia to ramp up concentrate exports ahead of ban
body: The firm has exported about 65% of the quota as of mid-August.

title: Indonesia president signals intention to go after illegal mines
body: Indonesia will move to “rectify” illegal mines estimated to have caused $19 billion in state losses.

title: Nickel surpasses coal as Indonesia’s top export, Macquarie says
body: Earnings from overseas sales of nickel products were $16.5 billion in the first half of the year.

title: Indonesia Aims to Dominate Global Nickel and Electric Vehicle Battery Industries Through Strategic National Nickel Management
body: Indonesia has the potential to become a major player in the global nickel industry, with over 700 million tons of nickel reserves and 54 smelter facilities, and is expected to produce 414,000 tons of nickel this year. However, the industry faces challenges such as reliance on imports, fluctuating prices, and regulatory issues, which the government needs to address to ensure the competitiveness of the national nickel industry.

title: Indonesian Government Evaluates B40 Biodiesel Program Implementation in the Mining Sector
body: The Indonesian government, through the Directorate General of New, Renewable, and Energy Conservation, is evaluating the implementation of the B40 biodiesel program in the mining sector, which has increased production costs by 3-5% for nickel miners amidst declining nickel prices. The evaluation aims to find solutions to ensure the program's sustainability, including considering flexibility in policy and supply chain issues, with industry associations calling for regular evaluations and involvement in the decision-making process.

title: Asosiasi Penambang Nikel Indonesia Evaluates B40 Implementation Amidst Industry Challenges
body: The Asosiasi Penambang Nikel Indonesia (APNI) has evaluated the implementation of B40, a program that has been in effect since January 2025, and noted a 3-5% increase in production costs in the nickel mining sector. The APNI has also reported delays in supply chains in several regions, including Sulawesi Tenggara, Sulawesi Tengah, and Maluku Utara, which have impacted operational efficiency.

title: Asosiasi Penambang Nikel Indonesia Releases Nickel Price Reference for September 2025, Showing a Decline from the Previous Period
body: The Indonesian Nickel Miners Association (APNI) has announced the Nickel Price Reference (HMA) for September 2025, with a price of US$ 14.899,64 per dry metric ton, representing a decrease from the previous period's price of US$ 15.012,67 per dmt. The association also provided detailed pricing for nickel ore with varying moisture content and nickel concentrations, ranging from US$ 28,37 to US$ 43,80 per wet metric ton.

title: Global Nickel Prices Remain Stable, Mixed Hydroxide Precipitate Sees Significant Increase
body: The Indonesia Nickel Price Index (INPI) reported stable global nickel prices, with Mixed Hydroxide Precipitate (MHP) experiencing a significant increase of $97 per metric ton to $12,883 per metric ton. The price stability and MHP increase reflect a balance between supply and demand, as well as growing demand from the Asian battery industry for electric vehicles, which is expected to drive production of high-value nickel products.

title: Indonesia Strengthens Inclusive and Sustainable Development Agenda Through Indonesia Energy & Engineering Series 2025
body: The Indonesia Energy & Engineering Series 2025, a multi-sector industry exhibition, aims to promote sustainability and industrial transformation, featuring over 2,000 participants from 42 countries and showcasing innovations in energy, infrastructure, and technology. The event supports the country's commitment to Net Zero Emission 2060 and highlights the importance of hilirisasi and efisiensi industri in achieving a green economy.

title: Indonesia's Nickel Industry Faces Trilemma in Implementing Environmental, Social, and Governance Standards
body: Indonesia's nickel industry is expected to face a trilemma of global demand, community price, and Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) standards, with companies like PT Vale Indonesia and Ceria Corp already implementing ESG standards and remaining profitable. The industry aims to achieve a win-win situation for all stakeholders through the implementation of ESG standards, with a focus on reducing carbon emissions, such as Vale's 28.7 ton CO2 per ton nickel intensity.

title: Indonesian Nickel Mining Sector Faces Challenges from Illegal Mining and Environmental Concerns
body: The Indonesian nickel mining sector is struggling with issues of illegal mining, environmental degradation, and social unrest, with 11 community members currently imprisoned for protesting against illegal mining activities. The Indonesian Nickel Miners Association (APNI) is working to address these challenges by implementing Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) principles and advocating for a more realistic and inclusive approach to decarbonization in the industry.

title: Nilai Ekonomi Karbon membuka peluang ekonomi baru dan meningkatkan efisiensi energi di Indonesia
body: Penerapan Nilai Ekonomi Karbon (NEK) di Indonesia dapat membantu pencapaian target iklim, meningkatkan efisiensi energi, dan mendorong adopsi teknologi rendah karbon, serta membuka peluang ekonomi baru melalui pasar kredit karbon dan penguatan daya saing industri. Dengan demikian, Indonesia dapat mengurangi emisi gas rumah kaca, meningkatkan ketahanan ekonomi, dan mempersiapkan industri menghadapi kebijakan internasional seperti Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM).

title: PT Bukit Asam Enhances Local Economic Empowerment Through Desa Impian Program With Local Heroes Approach
body: PT Bukit Asam's Desa Impian program has successfully empowered local economies, with 80 beneficiaries and a collective annual revenue of Rp3.05 billion, and has also reduced illegal mining practices by transforming non-productive land into integrated agricultural centers. The program has achieved significant results, including a 50% reduction in former illegal miners and a carbon emission reduction of 2.28 tons CO₂ per year, with plans to expand and integrate community products into a larger value chain.

title: Menteri Lingkungan Hidup Applauds PT Vale Indonesia's Progressive and Sustainable Environmental Investment
body: PT Vale Indonesia Tbk has been recognized for its commitment to environmental preservation, having reclaimed 3,800 hectares of land in Sulawesi and operated three hydroelectric power plants with a total capacity of 365 MW. The company has also successfully implemented a 3R principle for waste management, with 100% of non-B3 waste being reused or recycled in 2024.

title: BPMA Proposes New Initiatives for 2026 to Boost National Oil and Gas Development and Support Energy Transition
body: The Badan Pengelola Migas Aceh (BPMA) has proposed new initiatives for 2026, including a Rp3.9 billion allocation for exploration development in the North Sumatra Basin and Sibolga Basin, and a Rp4.5 billion allocation for monitoring and evaluating Carbon Capture Storage (CCS) and Carbon Capture Utilization and Storage (CCUS) in Aceh. These initiatives aim to accelerate national oil and gas development, support the energy transition agenda, and reduce carbon emissions in line with Indonesia's net zero emission target by 2060.

title: Indonesia's energy policy requires careful consideration to avoid mistakes that can have long-term consequences for the economy and the environment
body: The Indonesian government must make informed decisions regarding energy policy, avoiding mistakes such as inconsistent regulations and a lack of investment in renewable energy, which can lead to economic losses and environmental damage. A well-planned energy policy is crucial for the country's economic growth and environmental sustainability, requiring a balanced approach that considers the needs of the people, the environment, and the economy.
